correctness.rationale: PASS for the corrected RESULT.md only. The frozen unrestricted attainment statement in Limitations is false. With chi(s)=V(s)/m(s)^3, the integer certificate bounds chi(0.18)>0.169, chi(s)<0.168 for all s>=0.24, and Z(0.24)>1. Since chi tends to zero at both ends, it has a global maximum at some s0<0.24; hence L0=log Z(s0)>0 is allowed. At this field -H'' has its global minimum at rho=t(s0). Its weighted average along any nontrivial density interval starting at rho exceeds that minimum, since the curvature is analytic and nonconstant (including the endpoint intervals by a strict bound on an interior subinterval). So the extended quotient has its unique maximizing density at the excluded rho, and no measure attains C_L0. The replacement confines attainment to sufficiently large L and distinguishes the extended maximum from an attaining measure. Independently, Kac–Abramov and the one-return entropy bound cover measures with a zero atom (the extra term is s times the mass of the recurrent component, at most s); the iid lift yields equality and uniqueness at the pressure root. H''=-1/(t^3 V), and Gaussian moment estimates give p_L~(pi/4)e^{-2L}, rho_L~(pi/2)e^{-2L}, and C_loc~sqrt(2pi)e^{-L}. A curvature bound for t<=L^{-2} and the binary entropy bound above that cutoff exclude all maximizing sequences away from 1/2 as L grows. H' tends to minus infinity there, excluding the endpoint itself, so the maximum is attained off rho for large L. Stationarity gives (t+rho)(L-log Z)=2(s-p_L), first s/L→1/2 and then 2s-L=o(1). The length-5 term next to length 2 yields 1/2-t~(3/4)e^{-3L/2}. The entropy expansion H(1/2-d)=(2d/3)(log(3/(4d))+1)+O(d² log(1/d)) cancels the leading density loss in the quotient and leaves e^{-3L/2}/(2L²). The repaired statement preserves every strong-field coefficient, without an all-fields attainment inference.

value.rationale: The sharp observable-dependent constant measures the practical loss in using an infinitesimal susceptibility to predict departures from equilibrium. All optimizing measures in the strong-field limit are exponentially near the dense periodic orbit, not near the sparse equilibrium; the first correction measures the rare length-5 defects in that orbit. This is a substantive nonlocal boundary case for quantitative uniqueness, not a recalculation of the pressure or its derivatives.
residual_risks: One shift and one observable; no uniform Hölder result or general sparse-shift theorem is established.
